intended_object: A helper that rescales the first variable of a two-variable function: (x, η) ↦ F(R·x, η). I inferred this from the docstring and from its only use, in `constructed_prefix_bound`, where it feeds rescaled fields into `prefixJetSize_bound`.
explanation: The body matches the docstring exactly: it returns `F (R * p.1, p.2)`. This is the precomposition of F with the linear map diag(R, 1). The definition is a local device for the Navier–Stokes shape-transition argument. It lets the library state the smoothness lemma `scaledFamily_contDiff` and the prefix-jet estimate for fields whose first coordinate has been rescaled by the reset radius. It is not a standard notion from the literature, and Mathlib has no named counterpart; it would just be `F ∘ fun p => (R * p.1, p.2)`. So it is an auxiliary construction for a proof rather than a mathematical object to judge for faithfulness. As a helper it does what it says, with no degenerate-case problems: R = 0 simply gives the constant-in-x slice F(0, η).
